relationship.statement: A simple pendulum's period increases with the square root of its length and decreases with stronger gravity, while bob mass has no effect. Larger release angles widen the swing and slightly lengthen the period.
assumptions: The rod is massless and rigid, and the bob is a point mass.
Air resistance and pivot friction are neglected.
The formula applies closely for small angles under 15 degrees.

quantities.label: Rod length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot to the center of the pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the hanging bob, which tests whether heavier bobs swing faster.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration acting on the pendulum.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Initial angle from vertical where the pendulum starts swinging.

quantities.label: Swing period
quantities.meaning: Time required for one complete back-and-forth oscillation.

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of complete back-and-forth swings per second.

quantities.label: Angle
quantities.meaning: Instantaneous angle of the pendulum from the vertical over time.

quantities.label: Peak speed
quantities.meaning: Maximum speed of the bob at the lowest point of the swing.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = 1.5; var g = 9.81; var theta0 = 14 * Math.PI / 180; var omega = Math.sqrt(g / L); var period = 2 * Math.PI / omega; var frequency = 1 / period; var angleRad = theta0 * Math.cos(omega * t); var angle = angleRad * 180 / Math.PI; var max_speed = omega * L * theta0; var m = inputs.mass; var weight = m * g; var refWeight = g; var test_x = -0.5 + L * Math.sin(angleRad); var test_y = -L * Math.cos(angleRad); var ref_x = 0.5 + L * Math.sin(angleRad); var ref_y = test_y; var test_weight_y = test_y - (0.12 + 0.01 * weight); var ref_weight_y = ref_y - (0.12 + 0.01 * refWeight); var bob_size = 0.18 + 0.16 * m; var ref_size = 0.34; return { period: period, frequency: frequency, angle: angle, max_speed: max_speed, test_x: test_x, test_y: test_y, test_weight_y: test_weight_y, bob_size: bob_size, ref_x: ref_x, ref_y: ref_y, ref_weight_y: ref_weight_y, ref_size: ref_size, ref_angle: angle, weight: weight, is_lighter: m < 0.99, is_equal_ref: Math.abs(m - 1.0) <= 0.01, is_heavier: m > 1.01 }; }

lesson.title: Does bob mass change a pendulum swing?
lesson.description: Compare a variable test bob against a 1 kg reference pendulum of fixed length and gravity. Adjust the mass and watch the swing and angle graph.
lesson.instructions: Use the Bob mass slider to change the test bob from 0.5 kg to 5.0 kg. Compare its motion, weight arrow, and period against the 1 kg reference pendulum beside it.
lesson.goal: Bob mass increases gravitational force and inertia equally, so the pendulum swing period, angle, and peak speed stay unchanged.
